title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks fell Friday (Dow -271.9pts/-0.5% to 53,414; S&P 500 -0.4% to 7,718.60; Nasdaq -0.3% to 26,507) after August payrolls smashed forecasts (+162K vs +53K expected, unemployment steady at 4.1%), lifting odds of a Fed rate hike this month to ~58-59% from ~50%.
Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.79%; gold slid 1.3% to ~$4,481/oz; crude held near $91.32/bbl. Government bond yields in Japan, the UK and Germany hit multi-decade highs.
Companies: Volkswagen shares jumped 6.5% after its board approved doubling planned workforce cuts to 100,000 and halving its model lineup amid Chinese competition and tariff pressure.
Companies: Tesla fell more than 6% as its Austin Cybercab robotaxi launch (only 45 in service so far) left analysts with more questions than answers.
Companies: Flex agreed to buy EPC Power for $4.4B to expand data-center power offerings; China's Moonshot AI (maker of Kimi K3) hit a $50B valuation ahead of a planned Hong Kong IPO.
Macro/Policy: US diesel prices hit a record $5.85/gal, topping the 2022 high, as Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries tighten supply.
Macro/Policy: Trump threatened to cut off trade with deficit countries unless the Fed lowers rates; markets largely shrugged it off. US markets are closed Monday for Labor Day.
